transcript.text: Hi, I'm Sensei. Put your page under the camera and start solving. I'm watching.
You found the derivative of the outside function, but what happens to the inside function when you differentiate it?
Um, I dont know. Sin goes to cos, right? What do you mean the inside function?
Yes, sin goes to cos, but you need to use the chain rule for the inside function.
I dont really get the chain rule. Like what am I supposed to do with it?
The chain rule means you multiply by the derivative of the inside function. What is the derivative of 3x squared?
Um, 6x? So I multiply that by the cos thing?
Yes, 6x is correct. Now multiply that by cos(3x^2) to finish the derivative.
Okay so dy/dx is 6x cos of 3x squared, and at x equals 1 its 6 cos 3, about minus 5.94.
Got it. Give me a second.
Yes, you're on the right track. Now, what is cos(3) approximately?
Like minus 0.99, so yeah minus 5.94. Cool, thanks.
You're close, but you missed the chain rule part. Try again with the full derivative.
